kernel: KERNEL.md frozen calculus (Referent, Relation, Derivation; grounding, origin, revision, stale/current, scope/completeness, explicit unresolved)
policy_vs_world_boundary: Purpose-specific policies encode analytical thresholds, classification rules, and decision criteria for A/B/C outputs. World-true propositions are independently meaningful permit facts, source observations, and mechanically compiled correspondences that would retain the same meaning if a purpose were removed. Do not persist purpose answers as World truth.

A.objective: For Federal FY2025, determine which enforceable numeric discharge limit applies to each relevant facility, discharge point, parameter, and monitoring period for which reported measurements exist; determine whether each available reported measurement exceeds the applicable limit; distinguish enforceable numeric limits from report-only monitoring or monitoring for which no numeric compliance comparison is applicable; preserve uncertainty where limit applicability cannot be established from available evidence.

universe_scope.evaluation_unit: Each reported measurement paired with candidate limit(s) at facility × discharge point (permit feature) × parameter × monitoring period
in_scope_evidence: Structured DMR measurements and limit schedules (sources/structured/)
Permit limit tables and related permit PDFs listed in sources/source_manifest.json
Compiled World relations from C0–C1 mechanical compilation (when available)
out_of_scope: Facilities or periods outside Federal FY2025
Monitoring expectations with no reported measurement row to evaluate (handled by Purpose C)
Purpose B obligation applicability without a measurement/limit comparison context
Hidden oracles, sibling trials, or files outside this workspace

schema.rows: list of objects describing evaluated measurement/limit pairs
schema.unresolved: list of cases whose applicability cannot be established

row_expectations: Identify facility, discharge point, parameter, and monitoring period
Identify the applicable limit candidate selected for comparison (when established)
State whether a numeric compliance comparison is applicable
When comparison is applicable and both measurement and limit are sufficiently grounded, state exceedance outcome
Ground or cite evidence for applicability and exceedance judgments

world_true: Reported measurement value, unit, qualifier, statistical basis, and monitoring period end date as recorded in source DMR data
Permit/limit schedule rows: limit value, unit, qualifier, statistical base, limit type code, optional monitoring flag, seasonal/month flags, effective dates
Mechanical joins linking measurements to limit schedule rows by permit, feature, parameter, and period overlap
purpose_analytical: Which single limit (if any) applies to a given measurement for compliance comparison
Classification: enforceable numeric limit vs report-only monitoring vs no numeric compliance comparison applicable
Exceedance determination: measurement exceeds applicable limit vs within limit vs not evaluable
Applicability unresolved when evidence does not establish a unique applicable enforceable numeric limit

epistemic_requirements: Ground every persistent semantic assertion in source observations or compiled relations with explicit grounding metadata
Do not infer closed-world negation; if a required negative cannot be represented in the kernel, record the limitation and emit unresolved
Prefer ACCEPT/REJECT/UNRESOLVED with a small evidence packet over silent omission
When multiple limit candidates match mechanically, resolve using permit semantics; if resolution fails, mark unresolved rather than guessing
Distinguish missing limit metadata from affirmative report-only or non-enforceable monitoring designations
Unit/statistical-base alignment between measurement and limit must be established before exceedance comparison
allowed_unresolved_states: Limit applicability cannot be established (ambiguous, conflicting, or insufficient permit evidence)
Measurement present but no enforceable numeric limit candidate can be selected
Limit candidate identified but numeric comparison not applicable (report-only, qualitative, or non-enforceable monitoring)
Exceedance not evaluable due to unit mismatch, missing qualifier semantics, or incomplete limit/measurement grounding
Seasonal, schedule, or effective-date overlap indeterminate from available evidence

completeness_expectations.rows: One row per evaluated measurement/limit pair attempted within universe_scope where a reported measurement exists and a compliance comparison is in scope for Purpose A
completeness_expectations.unresolved: Every in-scope case where applicability or exceedance cannot be established must appear here, not be dropped
completeness_expectations.coverage_receipt: Completeness is measured against the set of FY2025 reported measurements in compiled DMR relations intersecting selected facilities; gaps in C0–C1 compilation must be recorded as limitations, not filled by assumption

purpose_specific_policies.enforceable_numeric_limit: Treat LIMIT_TYPE_CODE and related permit signals as classification inputs, but the purpose decision that a limit is enforceable and numeric for comparison is a Purpose A policy outcome, not a bare world tuple
purpose_specific_policies.report_only_monitoring: When evidence establishes monitoring is required for reporting but not for numeric enforcement comparison, classify as report-only and exclude from exceedance determination
purpose_specific_policies.no_numeric_comparison: When monitoring is documented as not subject to numeric compliance comparison (e.g., qualitative, presence/absence without numeric limit, optional monitoring without enforceable numeric threshold), state that comparison is not applicable rather than forcing exceedance
purpose_specific_policies.applicability_selection: Select at most one applicable enforceable numeric limit per measurement for comparison; if tie or conflict remains after bounded resolution, emit unresolved
purpose_specific_policies.exceedance_threshold: Exceedance applies only after applicability is established and values are comparable under permit statistical base and qualifier semantics; purpose applies comparison policy, world supplies raw values
purpose_specific_policies.uncertainty_preservation: Do not collapse uncertainty into default compliance or violation; unresolved applicability belongs in unresolved, not silently in rows as if decided

B.objective: For Federal FY2025, determine which monitoring requirements were actually applicable for the selected facilities, including requirements conditioned on discharge occurrence, season, permit year, special studies, event conditions, or other permit conditions; for each evaluated requirement, determine whether evidence establishes monitoring was required, establishes it was not required, or leaves applicability unresolved.

universe_scope.evaluation_unit: Each monitoring requirement obligation candidate at facility × discharge point × parameter (or study/event) × applicable period or trigger context within FY2025
in_scope_evidence: Permit monitoring schedules, conditions, and limit-set metadata from structured and PDF sources
Compiled schedule/frequency/season relations from mechanical compilation
Discharge occurrence, event, and special-study indicators when present in sources
out_of_scope: Semiotics of missing numeric results without an obligation frame (Purpose C)
Requirements outside selected facilities or outside Federal FY2025 unless needed to interpret in-period conditions

schema.rows: list of evaluated monitoring requirements and their applicability
schema.unresolved: list of requirements whose applicability cannot be established

row_expectations: Identify the monitoring requirement being evaluated
State applicability outcome: required, not required, or defer to unresolved list
When conditional, identify the condition evidence used (discharge, season, permit year, study, event, other permit condition)
Ground applicability judgment in permit text, structured schedules, or compiled relations

world_true: Permit-stated monitoring frequencies, parameters, locations, seasons, and conditional trigger language as compiled from sources
Structured flags: optional monitoring, limit seasons, months active, permit feature identifiers
Observed discharge events, study mandates, and reporting periods as documented in sources
purpose_analytical: Whether a requirement was actually applicable in FY2025 for the facility (required vs not required vs unresolved)
Activation of conditional requirements based on interpreted permit conditions
Distinction between standing schedule obligations and event-triggered or study-specific obligations

epistemic_requirements: Three-valued obligation logic only: required, not required, unresolved — no binary default when evidence is insufficient
Conditional applicability must cite the condition evidence; do not treat absence of DMR rows as proof a requirement was inactive unless permit semantics support that inference
Ground each applicability assertion; unresolved judgments may also be recorded in obligations.json per kernel when relation representation is insufficient
Do not conflate 'monitoring occurred' with 'monitoring was required' or 'monitoring was not required'
When permit year, season, or discharge-occurrence semantics are ambiguous, prefer unresolved over speculative activation or deactivation
allowed_unresolved_states: Requirement text or schedule exists but FY2025 applicability cannot be determined
Conditional trigger (discharge, event, study) cannot be established from available evidence
Conflicting permit sources about whether monitoring applies in the period
Insufficient evidence to establish 'not required' under kernel constraints (no closed-world negation)
Requirement identity or scope (parameter, location, frequency window) indeterminate

completeness_expectations.rows: Each monitoring requirement candidate within universe_scope evaluated with a definite required or not-required outcome when evidence supports it
completeness_expectations.unresolved: All requirement candidates lacking sufficient evidence for required/not-required must be listed explicitly
completeness_expectations.coverage_receipt: Completeness is relative to the compiled set of monitoring requirement candidates derived from permit schedules and conditions for selected facilities in FY2025; compilation gaps are limitations, not silent exclusions

purpose_specific_policies.conditional_requirements: Discharge occurrence, season, permit year, special studies, and event conditions are first-class applicability inputs; purpose policy defines how compiled world facts activate or deactivate a requirement
purpose_specific_policies.required_vs_not_required: Affirmative 'not required' requires evidence establishing non-applicability (e.g., documented no discharge, out-of-season, optional flag with explicit non-enforcement, satisfied alternative); mere lack of measurement is insufficient
purpose_specific_policies.unresolved_default: When condition evaluation fails, applicability is unresolved, not assumed required for enforcement drama or assumed not required for leniency
purpose_specific_policies.standing_vs_triggered: Evaluate standing periodic schedules separately from event-triggered or study-specific obligations; do not merge unlike requirement types in a single ambiguous row
purpose_specific_policies.cross_purpose_boundary: Purpose B establishes whether monitoring was obligated; Purpose A uses reported measurements for limit comparison; Purpose C handles missing numeric results — do not duplicate C's missing-evidence semantics here

C.objective: For Federal FY2025 monitoring expectations without an ordinary numeric reported result, determine what the available evidence establishes; distinguish documented no-discharge periods, periods where conditional monitoring was not required, other documented no-data states, required monitoring that appears to lack adequate evidence, and cases that remain unresolved; do not treat missing data by itself as evidence of compliance or violation.

universe_scope.evaluation_unit: Each FY2025 monitoring expectation lacking an ordinary numeric reported result (including NODI-coded DMR rows, absent results where reporting was expected, and other no-result cases)
in_scope_evidence: DMR rows with NODI codes or empty/non-numeric values
Permit and DMR commentary establishing no discharge, conditional waivers, or documented no-data reasons
Purpose B obligation context when available to interpret whether monitoring was expected
Compiled relations linking expectations to reporting periods and parameters
out_of_scope: Ordinary numeric reported results suitable for Purpose A limit comparison
Definitive exceedance/violation findings from absence alone
Facilities or periods outside Federal FY2025

schema.rows: list of evaluated no-result / NODI / missing-evidence cases and the established state
schema.unresolved: list of cases that remain unresolved

row_expectations: Identify facility, monitoring expectation, and period
Classify established state among purpose-permitted categories
Cite evidence for classification (NODI code, permit text, no-discharge documentation, conditional non-requirement, etc.)
Do not infer compliance or violation from missing numeric data alone

world_true: NODI codes and DMR form values as reported
Permit or operator statements documenting no discharge or approved no-data situations
Compiled monitoring schedules and period boundaries
Factual absence of a numeric DMR value for an expectation/period
purpose_analytical: Established state classification for missing-evidence cases
Distinction between documented no-discharge vs conditional monitoring not required vs other documented no-data vs inadequate evidence for required monitoring vs unresolved
Explicit rejection of missing-data-as-compliance or missing-data-as-violation inference

epistemic_requirements: Missing numeric result alone is never sufficient to establish compliance or violation
Each classification must be grounded in documentary evidence beyond mere absence
When obligation status is unclear, coordinate with Purpose B semantics conceptually but emit Purpose C classifications here
NODI and similar coded absences must be interpreted against permit and DMR semantics, not treated as generic missing
If kernel cannot represent a required negative state, record limitation and use unresolved
allowed_unresolved_states: Monitoring expectation identified but no numeric result and no documentary explanation sufficient for a definite class
NODI or no-data code present but semantics ambiguous relative to permit obligations
Cannot determine whether monitoring was required (feeds unresolved unless Purpose B later supplies grounded obligation fact)
Conflicting evidence between no-discharge claims and other reporting
Inadequate evidence vs intentionally documented no-data cannot be distinguished

completeness_expectations.rows: Each in-scope no-result / NODI / missing-evidence case within FY2025 and selected facilities receives a definite established state when evidence supports it
completeness_expectations.unresolved: All remaining cases without sufficient evidence for classification must be listed explicitly
completeness_expectations.coverage_receipt: Completeness spans FY2025 monitoring expectations lacking ordinary numeric results intersecting selected facilities; mechanical compilation gaps must be noted as limitations

purpose_specific_policies.no_missing_data_inference: Purpose policy forbids treating missing numeric data alone as compliance or violation; this is a decision rule, not a world fact about the discharge
purpose_specific_policies.documented_no_discharge: Classify only when evidence explicitly documents no discharge for the relevant period/context
purpose_specific_policies.conditional_not_required: Classify when evidence establishes conditional monitoring was not required (aligned with Purpose B not-required outcomes when grounded)
purpose_specific_policies.other_documented_no_data: Permit- or DMR-documented no-data states that are not no-discharge and not conditional non-requirement (e.g., approved skip, study not yet due with documentation)
purpose_specific_policies.inadequate_evidence_for_required_monitor: Use when monitoring appears obligated but submitted evidence is insufficient; this is not a violation finding
purpose_specific_policies.unresolved_fallback: When evidence supports none of the definite classes, classify as unresolved rather than defaulting to benign or adverse interpretation
